Composition and depth are inseparable. Without composition,
              depth becomes chaos—too many layers without hierarchy, just confusion. Without depth,
              composition feels weak—beautiful, but flat. A real cinematic image requires both:
              one to say where to look, the other to say where we are. Imagine a character alone on a bridge
              at sunset, placed using the rule of thirds, with negative space in the sky creating isolation, the bridge lines
              guiding attention, and mountains in the background adding depth. In a single frame, we feel space,
              emotion, direction, and story. That is cinematic design.

              both in slow motion.

c2f07fdb913b0179:
— “this matters” —
              slow-mo works in any genre, as long as something truly matters. In an action movie, it
              marks the decisive blow. In sports, the winning point. In an ad, the moment the product touches
              a hand or the transformation is revealed — the moment the brand wants to imprint on memory. In a music video, the
              emotional peak of the chorus. The content changes; the function is identical: tell the viewer where to look with their
              body, not just their eyes.
10b3270e87a86612:
“AI amplifies what already exists”: structure becomes more structure, chaos becomes more chaos. That’s why
          theory comes first — you establish what will be amplified.
